answer: An agent economy can make access to high-value jobs depend on a vertex’s accumulated, counterparty-signed work history: each completed task adds a signed edge from a real client, while duplicate identities cannot copy those attestations. A new identity starts isolated, like an island, and must earn trust through small jobs before reaching the garden of lucrative contracts. A Sybil attacker therefore pays in time and real labor for every identity, and must find independent clients willing to verify it.
